problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=3t\,i+2{t}^{3/2}\,j+4\,k,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by  $s=2(1+t)^{3/2}-2.$ Given that $R(s)$ is the parameterization of the given curve by its arc length $s,$ what is the $y$-component of $R?$

feedback.problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=⟨2t,\,1-3t,\,5+6t⟩$, $t\ge 0$, for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=7t.$ Find $R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, since $s=7t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{7}.$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $r(t)$ by its arc length $s$, with $s\ge 0$, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{7}) \\  & =⟨2(\frac{s}{7}),\,1-3(\frac{s}{7}),\,5+6(\frac{s}{7})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{7}⟨2s,\,7-3s,\,35+6s⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
